method: Actual unchanged SnowballSystem, Snowball/BigSnowball, Allocatable and bundled THREE in CPU VM. TextureLoader image I/O adapter, inert collision/effect/audio sinks and supplied clock. Native uses actual finish_frame with collision/AI/LocalLevel isolated.
changes: Per-shot stored shader time updated only when original Snowball.update runs; batched renderer receives each material time as float attribute instead of global current time.
Small and big material-state LIFO pools retain random/time on reuse; expiry caches updated time, pre-update collision retains old time.
Restart frees pending before active and retains class material-state pools across new game, consistent with original static Allocatable classes.
Dispatch leaves z NaN, mirroring Vector3.copy(Vector2) undefined z until first advance; renderer tests layer/visible eligibility rather than thrown tick. No claim about nonfinite GPU pixel behavior.
initialization_adapter: Native test imports random only for a source-verified fresh allocation; pool capacity/fresh decisions are checked before import. Reuse must retrieve stored native values. This does not certify whole-game UUID/RNG draw order.
cases: initial throw/new setup z undefined, later first advance finite
LIFO mixed-size setup, adjacent collision splice skip, newly parented but unupdated big snowball
hidden collided actor skipped for one update and per-material time retained
small/big reuse and old material clocks, bulk expiry splice skips
restart with active actors; restart with pending then active free order; reuse across new systems
limits: No renderer, GPU, browser/window, image readiness or OS input run.
Native pools random/time material state, not complete original object UUID, collider/event subscription/Splat component identity.
Source undefined z is represented by f64 NaN, compared as JSON null. Nonfinite clipping/driver behavior is unverified.
Source/native geometry, UV rotation and GPU transcendental differences are not established by state snapshots.
Whole-game clock synchronization, pooling aliases, native RNG/THREE UUID allocation order and scene routing remain partial.
